articleTitle: Modelling of Hybrid Electric Vehicle Charger and Study the Simulation Results
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Plug in Hybrid Electric Vehicles are driven by the energy stored in the battery. Through conductive AC charging method, Electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) is connected to Electric vehicle(EV) for charging the battery. Apart from charging it can also help in creating trustworthy equipment ground track and exchange control data among EV and EVSE. This paper discusses electrical and physical interface between EV and EVSE to facilitate conductive charging and design of an on-board charger for fast charging of the hybrid electric vehicle. The aim of this project is to design interfacing system between EV and EVSE as per automotive industry standard and to design prototype of 3.45 kw on-board charger using Matlab software. By modelling the charger, charging of Li-ion battery can be done which is used for providing propulsion torque and through various stages of charger voltage and current level is controlled and make them desired for charging.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Diffusion Based Unsharp Masking and Crispening for Denoising and Enhancement of MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: 1. Abstract-Unsharp masking and crispening of Magnetic Resonance Images (MRIs) is a vital factor for good visual inspection, accurate parameter estimation, and for further image processes like feature extraction and classification. To accomplish this objective, a method is proposed that is adapted from anisotropic diffusion filter(ADF). It utilizes ADF regularization as an intermediate step for smoothening of MRI image. It is an expanded and improved version of “Perona and Malik” Diffusion which gives a better image quality assessment when compares to other methods. The image quality assessment criterions like Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), mean square error (MSE) and structural similarity index (SSIM) are determined with respect to full reference image. Some no reference metric like Perception based Image Quality Evaluator (PIQE) and Blind/Reference less Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) are also determined. The corresponding results of full reference image for kaggle data-set. are estimated as 39.13dB, 7.21 and 0.99 respectively. The average result regarding for no reference metric are given as 48.84 and 37.13 respectively. The following outline has been executed in MATLAB R2015b which is used for MRI images of various resolutions, shape and size. The achieved outcomes expressed that overall image is deniosed & enhanced by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Hybrid Intelligence Technique for Reactive Power Planning using FACTS devices
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper designs and proposes a planning strategy of Reactive Power (VAR) in electric power transmission system. The proposed strategy primarily aims to minimize the total operating cost as well as real power loss of the system. In doing so, the advantages of hybrid intelligence techniques are used to elicit the optimal set of controlling parameters subjected to optimal power flow by managing the constraints. The FACTS devices are also installed according to their suitable place and size to compensate the reactive power flow through the transmission line. The positions for the FACTS devices are handled by different mathematical approaches. The ease of application, effectiveness as well as efficiency of the proposed approach is performed on a practical network pertaining in India.

articleTitle: Application of Quasi Opposition Based Whale Algorithm for LFC of Multi-area Deregulated Power System Using Fractional Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, novel Quasi Opposition based Whale Algorithm (QOWOA) is proposed for Automatic generation control (AGC) for two area interconnected power system with utilization of ultracapacitor. Both areas consist of thermal unit and Solar Field Unit. Non-Linearity such as Governor Dead Band (GDB) and Generation Rate Constraint (GRC) are employed in both areas. A modified PIDN-FOPD controller is used. A Novel QOWOA is proposed to optimize the gain parameters. System dynamics are studied by applying step load change (SLP). To validate superiority of proposed Algorithm dynamic response are compared with PSO. Robustness of proposed controller is compared with conventional PID controller. Distinct results rebuild the effectiveness of proposed work.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow with BAT algorithm for a Power System to reduce transmission line losses using SVC
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Due to drastic changes in society, leads to enhance the electricity demand in the entire world and increase the gap between generation and demand. This is one of the significant problems for electrical engineers to reduce the imbalance between the load and demand. For this purpose, add new generating units or use automation technology for better utilization of generating units which increases the use of fast and efficient algorithms. In this paper, real power losses minimization is treated as objective to optimize the active power generation, and it is achieved with the application of Bat Algorithm (BA). Through this nature-inspired algorithm, the control parameters such as real power generation at the PV buses, & the rating of Static VAR Compensator (SVC) are controlled. The output is more effective than other optimization techniques present due to the intrinsic properties of BA. The proposed BA for the single objective optimization is applied to the IEEE 30bus system.

articleTitle: Application of a Novel Political Optimization in Optimal Parameter Design of PI Controller for the BLDC motor Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: BLDC motors are getting popularity in recent times in various applications which necessitates an efficient speed control techniques. This paper proposes a speed control techniques for the BLDC motor by designing optimal parameters of PI controller using a novel political optimization (PO). The traditional methods of parameter design of the PI controller are complicated, and also these may result in large overshoot. Even though PSO based methods are widely used in literature to optimize the PI control parameters of the speed control of BLDC motor, these methods require the proper setting of more number of algorithm control parameters to get better performance. Hence, in this paper, a novel political optimization based optimal parameter design of the PI controller for the speed control of BLDC motor is proposed. The optimum values of PI control parameters are required for achieving the desired speed of the motor for any dynamic condition. A MATLAB/Simulink model of BLDC motor is used for testing the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Load Shifting Based DSM Strategy for Peak Demand Reduction in a Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: An electrical grid would be stable when the electricity demand and supply are in balance. The power generation should increase in response to increase in load. Demand-side management (DSM) is a way to reduce peak load demand so that adequacy of electricity will be maintained without interruption. Apart from reducing peak load demand, DSM is useful in other applications also, like mitigation of emergencies in the electrical power system, reducing blackouts and increasing reliability of the electrical power system. Due to these benefits, price of electricity reduces, harmful effects on environment also get reduced and also dependence on the conventional fuels reduces. In this paper, National institute of technology (NIT) Patna has been modelled as a micro grid for the reduction of peak/maximum demand through the use of available solar energy and implementation of load shifting based demand side management.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis For Wireless Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Downlink Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) supports massive wireless mobile devices, increases the spectral efficiency, and also supports the user-fairness, by multiplexing different users to share one wireless resource. In this paper, the analysis of signal outage for NOMA system in case of downlink has been analysed. Successive interference cancellation (SIC) technique has been analysed. Expressions of outage probability are obtained for different user in case of downlink NOMA system over Rayleigh fading channel. Also, the sum rate expression has been analysed. Finally, simulations has been done to confirm the expressions obtained for the different quantities. Also, sum rate comparison has been done to demonstrate the usefulness of this technique.

articleTitle: Stabilizing x -z Inverted Pendulum via Fractional Order PID Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, fractional order PID (FOPID) controller is implemented to stabilize x-z inverted pendulum (vertical inverted pendulum). Three FOPID controllers are used to control the angle and position (horizontal and vertical) of inverted pendulum. Mathematical model of the pendulum is used for designing the Simulink model and various parameters of the FOPID are obtained using the Whale optimization algorithm (WOA) technique. Simulation results obtained from FOPID is compared with PID controller. From the simulation results it is noticed that overall performance of the proposed controller is satisfactory with and without disturbances.

articleTitle: Integration of PV, Battery and Supercapacitor in Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Nowadays battery is used to stabilize the DC bus voltage but battery has low power density and high energy density. Whereas the supercapacitor has high power density but low energy density. So, for high energy and power density the integration of battery and supercapacitor is more efficient. It is more challenging to integrate the different sources. So it is required a control strategy to integrate the battery and supercapacitor and provide continuous power to the load. It has also shown that the battery and supercapacitor charged in access mode of power and discharged in deficit mode of power. In this paper proposed a new approach to control the power and dc bus voltage.

articleTitle: Equilibrium Optimized AGC of Multi-Area Restructured Power System Using Cascaded Fractional Fuzzy Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The focus of this work is to present an analytical study of cascaded fractional fuzzy controller (FPIDN-FOPI) to analyze its performance on automatic generation control (AGC) of two area four units restructured power system. AGC is a system, which adjusts output power and frequency change of a generator in the power plants, in response to sudden change in load demand. In this paper, two generating units are considered in each area consisting of thermal with reheat turbine and a gas generating unit. In order to make the system realistic thermal units are equipped with generation rate constraint (GRC). Controller gains are optimized by recently developed Equilibrium Optimizer (EO). System is subjected to step disturbance. Simulation results vindicate the utility of proposed controller by improving the dynamic response in comparison with the prevalent ones.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of the Gate Driver Circuit for Power Semiconductor Switches
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper elaborates on the structure and analysis of a novel gate driver circuit for an application of a single-phase five-level inverter system using IGBTs. The proposed technology contains a single-phase five-level inverter system with a novel isolated square wave gate driver for turning ON or OFF of IGBTs and MOSFETs. A six-channel gate driver is used in this topology where each circuit is provided with TLP250 optocoupler to get high output peak rating current to turn the switches On or Off. The design control algorithm for the operation of this single-phase five-level inverter application runs on an Arduino mega2560 microcontroller kit. The Arduino mega2560 microcontroller kit is used to generate the six-channel pulse with modulation of the scheme, with the frequency range about 2kHz.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modelling, Simulation and Control of Five-Phase Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a d-q transformation theory based mathematical model of five phase induction motor drive system. The control of drive is implemented using V/f control. This control methodology is capable to vary the speed of machine by controlling the frequency and amplitude of the stator voltage, such that the ratio of stator voltage to frequency keeps remains constant. This control for five-phase IM drive implemented in MATLAB, and simulation results reflect the validity of open-loop V/f control for 5-phase IM drive.

articleTitle: Siting and Sizing of DG Unit to Minimize Loss in Distribution Network in the Presence of DG Generated Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of optimal siting and sizing of a Distributed Generation (DG) unit in the distribution system in presence of DG-generated harmonics. Minimization of power loss in distribution network is often considered as the most desirable criteria for optimizing the location and size of DG. However, power electronic inverter based DG units inject harmonic currents into the network which in turn, distorts the bus voltages. IEEE Std. 519 has set a permissible limit of 5% on the maximum allowable voltage distortion. The maximum harmonic distortion in bus voltages in a network increases with increase in the size of DG and thus imposes restriction on the DG size at any given bus. Such restriction puts a limit on the amount of reduction in power loss that could have been achievable otherwise. Proper attention should be paid during optimal planning for DG size and location so that the targeted benefit can be maximized within the allowable limit of maximum voltage distortion. In this study, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)technique is applied to determine the optimal size of DG at any given bus that maximizes the reduction in power loss within the allowable limit of maximum harmonic distortions in bus voltages. Application of the proposed method on IEEE-33 bus system has been demonstrated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Grid Connected Photovoltaic Systems with Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Sun is a source of light since the dawn of civilization and researches has proven its promising and bright future as an alternative option to the most important conventional source of energy such as coal, gas and petroleum, which are getting depleted at an escalated rate. All around the globe researches are going on emerging environment-friendly renewable energy (RE) technologies. In this paper, a photovoltaic (PV) system of 100 kW rating is modeled in MATLAB/SIMULINK environment. Performance of the PV system along with adequate power electronic converter with AC load in standalone mode is analyzed and presented in the present work under changing environmental conditions. Incremental Conductance (IC) algorithm based maximum power point tracking has been adopted for maximum utilization of the studied PV system under different illuminations & panel temperatures. The present work also proposes the photovoltaic generation model in a grid-tied mode where the power is supplied to the isolated individual load and the inverter is usually controlled by a current mode control to deliver a sinusoidal voltage for the load.

articleTitle: Self-Supplied Automatic Control of Street Light
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents the way to utilize energy which is wasted when the vehicle passes over the speed breaker, and uses this energy to operate the automatic street light. The main focus in this field of technology is automation, power saving, and cost-effectiveness. Automation is set to reduce manpower with the help of an intelligent system. The main consideration is to save electric power because the traditional sources (Thermal, Hydro, etc.) are getting diminished due to various reasons. The ultimate goal of this project is to generate free energy and utilize it in an automatic street power system with LDR; this is to reduce power consumption. We want to save power by doing this automatically instead of manually. So, it's easy to make cost-effectiveness. So, in cities, towns, villages, etc. we can design an intelligent system for the usage of the street light.

articleTitle: Accommodative Energy Market for Battery Energy Storage and Grid Balancing
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electrical energy storage has a key role in offsetting variability and undependability of variable energy sources like wind and solar PV. The road to the economic viability of battery energy storage goes through accommodative and vibrant energy market and responsive regulatory framework that ensures level playing fields for emerging technologies. Battery storage technologies and their participation in various grid applications are linked to the economic viability of battery storage. Life cycle cost estimation using Monte Carlo Simulation to address the stochastic nature of input data of battery storage technologies for different grid applications will provide a common reference to assess their economic viability vis-à-vis conventional generators. Further compensation for different grid applications vary. Fast regulation services tailor-made for battery storage applications adopted by some independent system operators (ISO) will demonstrate economic viability and level playing field for battery storage technologies, and worth emulating policy paradigm for other ISOs.

articleTitle: Design of a High Gain DC-DC Converter for Renewable Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In recent times usage of renewable energy sources is emphasized through various technologies that are enhanced due to the shortage of conventional sources like coal, fossil fuel, etc. The high gain DC-DC converter is preferred for the conversion of low voltage which is obtained from PV/ wind energy systems to high voltage with less voltage stress on controlled power switch. In this paper, sudden (step) change in input voltage is shown as the energy that is obtained from PV/wind energy systems is not constant throughout the year. Here in the simulation the input voltage is varied from 9V to 21 V. Suitable selection and implementation of a coupled inductor topology are introduced which leads to improving the efficiency compared to the conventional DC-DC boost converter for sustainable operation in the long run. This topology is designed and simulated in MATLAB/ SIMULINK platform. Here the simulation is done for sudden change in load wattage (240W and 300W) and output voltage of the designed converter is kept nearly constant at 240V by the implementation of closed-loop control of the converter. It can be fed directly to the inverter for AC power generation which can be used for household appliances. Here coupled inductor is used in the proposed topology instead of transformer as it is more efficient and cost effective.

articleTitle: CNN Classifier based Low-resolution Face Recognition Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Faces captured under an uncontrolled environment usually have low-resolution (LR) in addition to poor illumination conditions and uncontrolled poses. These types of images significantly deteriorate the performance of traditional face recognition techniques. Hence, in this paper, a new face recognition algorithm is developed to minimize the problem of matching the LR images with high-resolution gallery images. In the proposed algorithm, the convolutional neural network (CNN) based classification mechanism is used to improve recognition accuracy. Investigational results performed on two standard databases of face images exposes the preeminence of the proposed algorithm over the other comparative existing face recognition models.

articleTitle: Effectivness of Space Vector PWM in Three-Phase Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This article represents the rule and application of Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation approach. This technique is advantageous over other modulation techniques. It supports more effective use of applied DC voltage in case of inverters. It causes less harmonic components in the output waveform. The comparative study of SPWM and SVPWM on the voltage source converter is performed in this article. The result is discussed and analyzed in MatLAB-Simulink domain.

articleTitle: Role of Demand Side Management in Automatic Load Frequency control
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper assesses the role of demand side management (DSM) in automatic load frequency control (ALFC) in presence of distributed generations (DGs). DSM has been introduced in ALFC in terms of demand response (DR). DR is introduced in the ALFC model of two area power system consisting of wind energy conversion system (WECS). The frequency regulation due to load variation is studied and better results are obtained after introduction of DR.

articleTitle: Investigation of Environmental Effects on the Performance of Solar PV Modules
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Now-a-days stipulation of energy all over the world is increasing and different types of renewable energy have been developed. But among all, the photovoltaic (PV) system has been proven to be the best energy generating source. The solar energy conserved by solar cell doesn't produce any kind of pollution and has negligible side effect. But the environmental factor like wind, dust, humidity, heat, moisture, etc affects the efficiency of power generated by the solar cell. These are the disturbances that act as challenge for the solar cells. So, the objective of this paper is to examine the PV system which is affected by factors like: dust deposition, presence of moisture (on it) and the changes of environmental heat. All the important parameters - current and voltage - have been noted down and compared by using the characteristic curve. The differences between energy generation with and without the disturbances have been observed.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Approach for Reactive Power Compensation in an Active Distribution Network with Wind Based Renewable Integration
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The paper presents a heuristic method for locating proper sites / buses for shunt compensation in an active distribution network containing wind turbines considering a multiobjective criterion. The strategy is applied for demonstrating the uncertainties associated with the dynamic load demand and stochastic nature of wind speeds using the Monte-Carlo Simulation. The voltage profile improvement has been considered as one of the objective of the work. The same is achieved by shunt compensation and the second objective is formulated to minimize the amount of shunt compensating element. Two case studies have been considered one with a single shunt capacitor and the other with two shunt capacitors. As both the objective function are contradictory to one another, so a simultaneous optimization is carried out using Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-III. Using the values of the parameters obtained from the adopted data, the method has been tested on a 69 bus radial distribution network.

articleTitle: Dynamic participation of DFIG based wind farms for improved frequency regulation
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents the dynamic participation of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) based wind power generation in the proposed frequency regulation framework. An attempt has been carried out to study the impact of DFIG for the system dynamic responses. Maiden cascaded Tilt Integral - Tilt Derivative (TI-TD) controller is designed for the investigated system. A novel Opposition-Based Path Finder Algorithm (OPFA) is proposed for obtaining different optimal gain parameters of the intended controller. Comparison with some other controllers validate the efficacy of the designed controller. Finally the distinct improved results under random load perturbation demonstrate the effectiveness of the conceived approach.

Author Keywords: Cascaded Tilt Integral- Tilt Derivative (TI-TD) Controller

articleTitle: Fish Freshness Assessment using NIR spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The feasibility of near- infrared (NIR) spectroscopy to discriminate the freshness of an Indian Major Carp, Rohu (Labeo rohita) was investigated in this paper. The spectroscopic readings of Rohu samples were recorded for the wavelength range between 900 and 1700 nm in absorbance mode. The Principal Component Analysis (PCA) was applied to analyze the spectral data and distinguishable clusters were obtained. Study revealed that, the freshness of the Rohu could be distinguished by NIR Spectroscopy. The Separability Index (SI) of the raw data was also measured as 873.7008. Preliminary results showed that, this technique could be applied for discrimination of Rohu fish freshness.

articleTitle: A new generalized topology for multilevel inverter with reduced number of DC sources and switches
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper a new generalized single-phase multilevel inverter (MLI) with minimum number of DC sources and switches is proposed. This proposed topology of single phase MLI can also be extended for three phase system. Isolated photovoltaic (PV) modules may also be employed as DC source. Thus, this MLI keeps the benefits of conventional cascaded H bridge (CHB) inverter. In this topology combination of DC sources and capacitors are used. There is no problem of balancing of capacitors voltages in the proposed MLI. Concept of optimum load sharing is also utilized in this paper. This MLI works for different range of R-L load. Simulation model for the proposed topology is developed in MATLAB/SIMULINK and finally their results are discussed for analysis purpose.

Author Keywords: Alternate phase opposition disposition pulse width modulation (APOD-PWM)

articleTitle: Novel Reduced Switch 9-Level DC/AC Converter With Unequal Sources
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents A novel structure of reduced switch multi-level voltage source inverter. The proposed topology use minimum number of switching device and voltage source to produce 9-level output voltage with less total harmonics distortion (THD). The gate pulses are generated using sinusoidal pulse width modulation technique (SPWM) to turn on the semiconductor devices. Based on the switching strategy the the proposed model is able to developed 9-level (0, ±Vdc/2, ±Vdc, ±3Vdc/2, ±2Vdc) output voltage. The simulation is performed on MATLAB/Simulink environment for reduced switch 9-level VSI, the converter is tested on resistive and inductive load. Based on simulation result the proposed technique is recommended for good performance in term of total harmonics distortion and cost of overall system.

articleTitle: Impact of Renewable Sources in AGC for Two Area Interconnected Power System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The integration of non-conventional energy sources like wind energy for economical operation is not just increasing the size of the modern power system but also the complexity in meeting the load demand. Hence, a better control scheme and optimization technique is required to maintain the system equilibrium. In the current paper, a two interconnected area electrical power system (both the areas comprising of a hydro power plant, thermal power plant, gas power plant and doubly fed induction generator (DFIG)) has been analyzed. A Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller with a derivative filter has been used to manage the damping in the system. Further, a new meta-heuristic Hybrid Salp Swarm Differential Evolution Algorithm (HSSDEA) optimization technique has been used to optimize the controller gain.

articleTitle: Multi-point Optimal Placement of Shunt Capacitor in Radial Distribution Network: A Comparison
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Reactive power compensation is very vital for optimal operation of transmission and distribution system. Series and shunt capacitor banks and flexible alternating current transmission systems (FACTS) are the solution for optimizing the transmission and distribution system. Out of these, shunt capacitor banks are frequently utilized in distribution network for voltage enhancement, power factor improvement and system's technical loss reduction. This article presents a technique for optimal placement of shunt capacitor banks in distribution systems based on electrical centrality index. “Centrality” is graph-theoretic index which identifies imperative node within a network and it has been used in proposed method for locating suitable site for shunt capacitor banks. The planned method is realized in 34-bus radial distribution test network and demonstrates its comparison with existing method as well.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Reduction of BLDC motor introducing Delay in the Gate Firing Circuits
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electric vehicle is an important component in any smart city and Brushless DC (BLDC) motor is an obvious choice for an electric vehicle. But most of the existing technology of BLDC motor drive suffers from a significant amount of torque ripple. In this paper reduction of torque ripple in Brushless DC motor is studied and a technique has been proposed to minimize it. In a conventional three phase Brushless DC motor with 120° conduction mode torque ripple occurs at 60° interval. i.e. six times in a complete cycle. Torque ripple occurs due to change over of load current from one phase to the other. In this paper an OFF delay has been introduced in the gate firing circuit of the inverter which feeds the brushless DC motor and minimizes the torque ripple. Also this delay has been presented as a function of speed by which the OFF delay can be predetermined to be incorporated in the gate circuit. The propped topology is verified using a suitable computer simulation in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Discretization of Linear Time-Varying Systems
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper discusses the exact discretization of linear time-varying (LTV) systems. Usually, Taylor series based methods are used for exact discretization of the continuous-time systems. The extended versions of Taylor based methods have been reported in recent years for nonlinear systems as well but they have been found to be ineffective in case of LTV systems. The reason of avoiding Taylor based methods for exact discretization has been discussed in this article and an alternative method has been proposed. This is an integration approach based method for obtaining the exact discrete version. Illustrative examples shown here, discusses the effectiveness of proposed method and presents comparative analyses for exact discretization.

articleTitle: Impact of back-gate voltage on sensing metric of dielectric modulated Tunnel FET biosensor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the effect of back-gate voltage on sensing metric of Dielectric Modulated (DM) Tunnel Field Effect Transistor (TFET) biosensor. Under this work we have investigated transfer characteristics, the variation of energy band, and hole concentration with back gate voltage and calculated the drain current sensitivity and selectivity for three different value of back-gate voltage. In this work, we have shown that with positive back gate voltage, drain current sensitivity is improved by nearly one order of magnitude and selectivity value is also enhanced by more than 2 times.

articleTitle: Wind Generation Forecasting Using Python
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Wind generation forecast shows a dynamic part in renewable energy production. Authentically wind generation forecasting is exceptional challenge because of undetermined and composite efforts of wind signals. That's the reason, faithful forecasting techniques are necessary. This paper shows linear regression-based machine learning technique to discover the underlying relationship between wind data and to predict exact wind generation. Regression concern to wind data to withdraw the invisible characteristics from wind data to recognize purposeful particulars. It's also has been utilized to draw out greater interconnection between the values. The proposed plan is implemented to 3 dissimilar datasets (hourly, monthly, & yearly) collected through the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) to modify power database. The forecasted outcome appear that the projected investigation can correctly forecast wind energy by means of a spread range from hour to years. A contrast is made with well linked state of the art method and it is illustrated that the proposed investigation yields superior forecasts outcomes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Parallel-Connected Grid Independent Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In grid independent Wind Energy Conversion System, the chance of a mismatch between available wind power and user demand is very high. Therefore, such systems are equipped with an energy storage device like a battery for a typical grid independent system being used even in this research activity. In this paper, mathematical models like Wind Turbine (WT), Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG), Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller etc. are built for Wind Energy Conversion System in Saber-RD simulator. The real-time issues observed in parallel-connected wind systems are overloading of PMSG and one of the turbines (out of two) running at higher speed over the other because of which unequal power sharing that occurs while feeding the battery. Certain other issues have been investigated through the modeling and simulation of a given WECS which are crucial to the understanding, analyzing & solving issues faced when more than one WECS each rated 5.1kWp are parallel operated. Such practical systems termed Hybrid (Wind+ Solar) Renewable Energy Systems built on the roof tops of 3 GVP Institutions have been in operation for the last 4 years as grid independent systems. Based on the investigations, it is found that the addition of inductance as a function of synchronous inductance in series with one or more of several PMSGs (Permanent Magnet Synchronous generator) is cost effective to solve the problem of unequal power-sharing while feeding battery storage. The article discusses the validation of such simulation results derived from the sub system models are first validated for given Wind Energy Conversion System and extended to two systems to find the cost-effective solution for issues faced in the operation of such multiple (two in this case) system.

articleTitle: An Improved 3-Phase Load Flow for DG Integrated Distribution Systems Based on PSO
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The recent trend of integrating distributed generation (DG) units with distribution network has necessitated reformulation of conventional distribution load flow problem to incorporate the DG models. 3-phase distribution load flow with DG models included, has already been reported by a number of authors. These studies, however, suffer from two major drawbacks. Firstly, the allocation of active and reactive power outputs among the three phases of the DG units under unbalanced loading conditions of the systems could not be properly considered in these studies. Under such operating conditions, loading of the three phases of a DG unit is more likely to be unequal. But, in these studies, the active and reactive power outputs of the three phases of the DG units had been allocated equally among the three phases of those units. Secondly, the solutions provided by these studies can not ensure balance in the 3-phase internal voltages of the DG units, which is an essential requirement arising naturally due to design of 3-phase DG units and the available methods of their control. The present work applies Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to develop an improved methodology for 3-phase distribution load flow to alleviate the above mentioned drawbacks. The results of application of the proposed load flow on IEEE 13 node network and on IEEE 25 node network have been presented in support of the claim made by the present authors.

articleTitle: Detection of Curcumin using a Simple and Sensitive Molecularly Imprinted Polymer (MIP) Embedded Graphite Electrode Based Electrochemical Sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, polyacrylic acid based molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) was synthesized for detection of curcumin. The polymer materials were prepared by polymerization process using curcumin (CUR) as the template molecule and acrylic acid (AA) as a monomer. The electrochemical behavior of curcumin was investigated using three electrode system in the presence of ammonium acetate buffer solution with pH value of 5.5. The polymer materials were characterized by ultraviolet-visible spectroscopy (UV-Vis). The effect of scan rate variations was examined and the principal component analysis (PCA) was implemented for qualitative analysis of five different samples. The separability index (SI) was observed 23.29 with effective data clustering. This method can be also applied effectively for similar applications.

articleTitle: Reduced Graphene Oxide/Amino-Nitroso-Uracil Nanocomposite for the Detection of Heavy Metals in Aqueous Environment
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The rGO-ANU composite has been synthesized via hydrothermal method. The composite material was characterized using FTIR, UV-vis spectroscopy, XRD and SEM. SEM analysis showed well exfoliated rGO in rGO-ANU composite. The composite was applied for the detection of the heavy metal using the UV-vis spectroscopy method. Among the series of metals, Ag<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> has been found sensitive against the composite material with detection limit of 3.69 μM and quantification limit of 12.3 μM in an aqueous medium.

articleTitle: Discrimination of Various Clones of Black Tea Using NIR Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, discrimination of five different clones of black tea viz., TV 20, TV 18, TV 22, TV 23 and mixed clone (a mixture of TV 20, TV 18, TV 22a and TV 23) has been described using near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). The absorbance spectra of the black tea samples were recorded in the wavelength window of 900 - 1700 nm. Each type of black tea samples provided a signature which has been evaluated using principal component analysis (PCA). For quantitative evaluation of the data nature, class separability index (SI) has been calculated. SI value obtained for the raw NIR spectral data was found to be 17.32 which reflect good separability. Additionally, the distinct and segregated clusters so formed in the PCA score plot using the NIR spectral data reveals that the five clones of black tea can clearly be distinguished using NIR spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Interactive Search Algorithm Based Automatic Generation Control Using Cascade Control and UPFC
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study deals with the automatic generation control of two-domain diverse source system. Each domain is constituted of a distributed generation constituent, a gas constituent and a thermal constituent. Further UPFC is connected with the transmission-line to enhance the dynamics of the network. Interactive search algorithm is used to optimize the cascade controller used for the secondary control of the proposed structure. The simulation result divulges the efficacy of the presented control methodology and the overall supremacy of the network when UPFC is integrated with the transmission-line.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of HVDC Lines Using Surge Arrester
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The paper shows a comparative harmonic analysis with surge arrester as well as without surge arrester at the inverter side for LCC (Line Commutated Converter) based HVDC system. Harmonic analysis has been done based on both conditions i.e. with and without surge arrester. The voltage, current as well as threshold values are analysed and it is compared for two conditions. With the help of FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) analysis, better comparison results are obtained. A DC line connecting the two three-phase sources has a length of 800 km. With the help of Matlab/Simulink, the results have been obtained.

articleTitle: Scalar Control of Induction Motor Drive with Inverter Fault-Tolerance Capability
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, a three-phase induction motor drive with inverter switch fault-tolerance capability is proposed. The voltage balance issue in the traditional fault-tolerant converter topology (B4) is resolved by using single capacitor at the dc-link in the proposed fault-tolerant converter topology. The boost converter is controlled by current control technique and induction motor is controlled by scalar V/F control. These two control strategies give appropriate switching states to get regular operation of the motor in healthy and post-fault condition. Experimental results are presented to demonstrate the proposed scheme and its control. Also, a comparison with the available fault-tolerant converter schemes is given to show the merits of the proposed converter topology.

Author Keywords: current control and induction motor drive

articleTitle: Gain-Scheduled Feedback Controller Design for a Nonlinear Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Gain-scheduled Composite Non linear Feedback (CNF) control has been implemented to Continuous Stirred Tank Reactor (CSTR) in this work. Chemical reaction takes place inside the CSTR, which is adjured from high residual concentration to low residual concentration. Control of CSTR is a bit complex, as it requires complete dynamic study and its implementation. During the entire process, the reaction kinetics changes from stable-unstable-stable range with the decrease in residual concentration. To stabilize the reaction, appropriate cooling is necessary, to ensure that overheating of the CSTR doesn't occur. Gain-scheduled composite non linear feedback controller has been implemented successfully for better tracking performance and error has been computed in terms of Integral of Absolute Error (IAE). The novelty of the work lies in lesser error obtained for this particular model of CSTR. Comparison of the IAE has been done with Model Reference Adaptive Control (MRAC) MIT control in CSTR.

articleTitle: Impact of Distributed Generation on the Reliability Allocation of Distribution System: A mesh-Grid Approach
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The power system has a basic function to provide the electrical energy to the customers in a safe, economical and reliable way. The presence of distributed generation in power system network not only acts as emergency shelter but also improves the overall reliability of the system. It serves as a support to keep the system intact. This paper illustrates the consequence of distributed generation on the reliability allocation of the IEEE 33 and 69-bus distribution system. The main objective is calculating the reliability of the mesh-grid representation of the network and improving the reliability by allocating a targeted reliability value. The need for performance enhancement of power system components with a reduction in cost contribute to allocation. A comparative study of sensitivity analysis on the basis of component failure rate and network configuration is assessed for its reliability improvement and making the microgrid self-sustainable.

articleTitle: Single-Phase Average Reactive Power Measurement Using Instantaneous Power Theory in a Fixed Point Processor
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Nowadays, in AC power systems, reactive power and its measurement are important factors, as these affect the system efficiency. A number of measurement techniques have been developed using quadrature phase shifting circuit, wavelet transform, Hilbert filtering, integration-differentiation method etc. A new technique of average reactive power measurement in a single phase AC circuit using instantaneous power theory has been presented in this paper. This is based on a simple algorithm using instantaneous power concept in α-βreference frame. Any complicated calculation like integration etc. has been totally avoided. The technique is applicable for generic voltage and current waveforms. The algorithm is validated via simulation in a digital platform and via experimentation, using an inexpensive mid-level 8-bit fixed-point processor.

articleTitle: Estimation of Theophylline in Black Tea Using NIR Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The present work delivers a study on evaluation of biomarkers present in tea using NIR spectroscopy. Three primary biomarkers theophylline, theobromine, L-theanine found in black tea have immense benefits toward human health. The NIR spectral data for each pure compound of different molarity were examined. The NIR spectrometer experiment was performed in transmission mode within the range of wavelength 900-1700 nm. Chemometrics was imposed for detailed spectral data analysis. Three different compounds were analyzed and distinguished using principal component analysis (PCA). Effective clustering of three compounds was noticed from the PCA plot. A high measure of class separability index for NIR data obtained has been found to be 41.6. The biomarker theophylline was subjected to quantitative prediction and correlation using partial least square regression (PLSR) analysis. Prediction algorithm provided correlation factor of 0.81 with a high value of average prediction accuracy 92.62%. Based on the primary investigation it can be stated that the NIR spectroscopy technique may be implemented for the assessment of different biomarkers present in black tea.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Different Converter Topologies for an SRM Drive with Conventional and Vector Control Schemes
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The SRM drive has started slowly penetrating into the competitive drive market. For its further acceptance its limitation needs to be overwhelmed. The big issue with SRM being its noisier operation which is due to the type of excitation current utilized in the machine drive. In this paper nonconventional type of excitation current is utilized in an SRM drive on the basis of which the vector control strategy under MTPA control is tested. The machine drive is tested for both conventional control and vector control schemes with different converter topologies and a comparison is made between them on the basis of percentage current THD.

articleTitle: SOS Based Solution for Optimization of Indian Power System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a Symbiotic Organisms Search (SOS) algorithm based solution to optimize the control variables simultaneously to optimize the power system real power loss and voltage stability limit. This issue can be mathematically formulated as a problem of nonlinear equality and inequality limited optimization, with an objective function integrating real power loss and voltage stability limit. The problem formulation included transformers taps, unified power flow controller and its parameters as control variables. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm has been tested on Indian 24-bus system. The simulation results obtained with the proposed algorithm are compared with the real coded genetic algorithm (RCGA) for a single objective of minimizing real power loss and multi-objective minimization of real power loss and maximization of voltage stability. Results from simulation demonstrate the ability of the proposed algorithm in solving the optimization problem.

articleTitle: A Novel Optimization Technique for LFC and Virtual Inertia Emulation of a Multi Area Hybrid Power System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Frequency regulation is one of the important power quality issues of an interconnected power system. Load Frequency Control (LFC) is a classic approach for frequency regulation of the power system. The optimization techniques, used to optimize the parameters of controller used in LFC mechanism plays a vital role. On other hand, integration of Distributed Generation (DG) systems and corresponding power electronic converters ruins power system inertia. Through restoring inertia of the power system, improvement in the rate of change of frequency can be accomplished. This article discusses derivative based virtual inertia emulation technique using Energy Storage System (ESS) and its impact on power system's frequency regulation. At the same time, a new effective optimization technique, named Opposition Based Volleyball Premier League (OVPL) algorithm is used to optimize the essential parameters of controller and ESS. The effectiveness of the proposed work has been examined by deploying for a two area interconnected hybrid power system including nonlinearities. The performance of proposed algorithm is verified by comparing with several recent optimization techniques. The robustness of the work against wide range variation of power system model parameters.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Converter Topology for Speed Control of Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A voltage source inverter (VSI) with three-level boost converter (TLBC) at its front end is proposed for fault tolerant operation of three phase induction motor drive to achieve uninterruptable speed control for various load conditions. Current control is used for TLBC and scalar V/F control is used for induction motor. Results for real-time control are presented to highlight the merits of the proposed converter topology when compared with conventional fault-tolerant converter (B4).

articleTitle: Load Frequency Regulation using Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control Technique
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper a Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) technique is utilized to control the fluctuation in frequency for single area and two- area interconnected power system. LADRC consists of feedback controller and Extended State Observer. The total disturbance comprising of internal ambiguity and external perturbation in the plant is estimated in real time with the help of ESO and these estimated total disturbance is compensated by feedback controller. The parameters of LADRC are simplified into two bandwidths using pole placement technique i.e. observer bandwidth and controller bandwidth. The Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm is utilized to find out these two bandwidth and then the optimized value is used in LADRC controller. The effectiveness of the proposed LADRC technique in LFC problem is authenticated by the recently reported technique in the literature. The disturbance rejecting capability and the robustness toward the parameter variations of the proposed method are also shown by the extensive simulation results.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Brushless Direct Current Motor Drive for Different types of DC-DC Converter Using MPPT
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Furtherance in power semiconductor devices material and fabricating technology has accredited the design of extremely efficient and compact motor drives. This paper proposes a power converter implementation of Brushless DC motor drive system with solar photovoltaic array. A maximum power point tracking algorithm called incremental conductance method is served to exploit the maximum power of PV array. Implementations of the BLDCM in the boost, zeta and modified zeta converter have been done and motor parameters (rotor speed, electromagnetic torque and stator back EMF) are discussed. The three topologies are compared based on the parameter values. MATLAB/SIMULINK is used to design and simulate the desired configuration.

articleTitle: Path Planning of UGV using Sampling-Based Method and PSO in 2D Map Configuration: A Comparative Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The navigation system of an unmanned ground vehicle is a core research area in the field of robotics. It must be robust enough to guide UGV from source to destination through an obstacle free path. Nowadays many research are going on path planning algorithms both in a static and dynamic environment. In this paper a comparative work has been presented between sampling-based technique algorithm (PRM, bidirectional RRT) and particle swarm optimization algorithm applied in a static simple and complex environment. Sampling-based techniques use random sampling for the selection of points in the configuration space while checking not to be in obstacle configuration. The results showed that both types of techniques generated obstacle-free path in different periods. The time required by sampling-based technique is relatively less than the PSO technique. In sampling-based technique the path has vertexes at the sampled points while in PSO path consists of smooth curve which can be changed in the algorithm.

articleTitle: Robust Least Square Filter for Simultaneous Localization and Mapping
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, a robust least square filter (RLSF) based simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has been presented. First a RLSF for nonlinear systems has been derived using the concept of extended Kalman filter design. For designing the filter, system uncertainties have been considered in the system model. This kind of filter may be useful in the field of robotics and fault diagnosis. Then the derived filter has been applied to SLAM for evaluating its performance and applicability. Finally the proposed method is simulated in MATLAB with numerical data and compared with EKF based SLAM. It is found that the present method is performing better than EKF based SLAM.

articleTitle: Single-channel color image cryptosystem using chaotic structured phase encoding
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A new single-channel color image cryptosystem using chaotic structured phase mask (CSPM) is proposed to circumvent silhouette problem by two ways. In this scheme, HL, LH, and HH sub-bands of a gray-scale carrier image are replaced with R, G, and B channels of an input color image and then inverse discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is employed to produce a single-channel color image, which is inverse gyrator transformed. The input image is hidden into three phase-only-masks (POMs), which can be allocated to three authorized users for a secure authentication system. The CSPM as third POM contains multiple asymmetric keys. The viability and security of the proposed system have been validated by numerical simulations experiments.

articleTitle: S-Transform Assisted CUSUM Based Protection Strategy for Transmission Lines Possessing UPFC
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The different operating modes of unified power flow controller (UPFC) affect the voltage, current and hence the measured impedance at the relay location both during steady-state and transient conditions. As a result, the conventional distance relay based on fixed impedance setting finds difficulty in protecting the UPFC compensated transmission line (TL). In this paper, the effect of UPFC on distance protection is studied explicitly and a Fortescue and Stockwell transform based fault detection and classification scheme is proposed. The functioning of the proposed technique is evaluated by simulating data for different fault cases on a 400 kV two-bus and double circuited UPFC installed power system through EMTDC/PSCAD software. The fast and accurate results for the proposed scheme clearly justify the efficacy of the proposed relaying technique for UPFC compensated line.

articleTitle: Investigation of Buffer less Cu2ZnSnS4 Based Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Cadmium Sulphide ( CdS) is a prominent buffer layer used in various kesterite based solar cells. However, toxicity of CdS has created an urgent need to search for alternate buffer layers. In this work, Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>ZnSnS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> (CZTS) based solar cell, is simulated using SCAPS-1D software, by removing CdS buffer layer, to reduce toxicity and increase efficiency of the solar cell, simultaneously. Aluminium doped ZnO is used as a transparent conducting layer along with Mg-ZnO which acts as both buffer and window layer. The swapping of CdS by Mg-ZnO has been done to investigate the open-circuit voltage, short circuit current density, fill factor, and efficiency of the solar cell. The efficiency of 12.16% has been confirmed using this new buffer less CZTS based solar cell.

articleTitle: Effect of Change in Environmental Factors on Coordination of Overcurrent Relays with DG Integration
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: With the increase in Distributed Generation (DG) in distribution systems to maintain the reliability of the supply, there occurs problem of relay coordination. Therefore, it has become important to address this issue as it has become a big challenge for the power system protection engineers. With the incorporation of DG, the radial nature of distribution system is lost and short circuit level is also increased therefore, it leads to maloperation of relays as the previous settings of the relays needs to change. The goal of this paper is to address the issue of relay coordination at different wind speeds encountered by wind turbine. GA and PSO optimization techniques are applied to achieve optimum coordination of over-current relays in a three bus system with a detailed model of wind used as Distributed Generation. MATLAB and SIMULINK have been used for all programming and simulation requirements.

articleTitle: LFC Scheme for A Deregulated Multi-Area Power System using Cascaded Fractional Order Controller
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Active power imbalance between electrical power generation and demand causes deviation in frequency and tie-line power of an interconnected power system. Load Frequency Control (LFC) is an epoch-making method to maintain nominal frequency and tie-line power of a power system. Also, continuous research is going on to improve the effectiveness of the LFC mechanism. In this scenario, this paper contributes to design an effective controller configuration for LFC mechanism of a nonlinear multi area interconnected system. A cascaded combination of Proportional-Integral controller with Fractional Order Proportional-Derivative controller (PI-FOPD<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>N) has been proposed in this work. One of the popular whale optimization algorithm (WOA) has been deployed to optimize the proposed controller parameters. The proposed scheme has been compared with several conventional controllers and its robustness has been checked by subjecting it to variation in power system model parameters. Deregulation environment of power system is also incorporated for more realistic approach.

articleTitle: Effect of applied bias on Schottky interface to affect resistive switching in a memristive device
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Resistive Random Access Memories (RRAMs) or Memristor has been a revolution in current nonvolatile memory technology. This work demonstrates an analytical model that shows the effect of applied bias on the metal-semiconductor interface to affect resistive switching of an RRAM device. The applied bias modulates the corresponding interface in terms of various interfacial electrical parameters. Besides, the change in bias affects the distribution of bulk defects primarily oxygen vacancies as well as non-lattice oxygen ions. This, in turn, also affects the corresponding resistance of bulk as well as other electrical parameters at the interface. Further conduction mechanism of the device with interfacial oxide formation as well as dissolution to impact resistive switching behavior has been elaborated.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Electrically Exploding Wire Opening Switch for Pulse Compression
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Pulse Shaping Network (PSN) conditions the electrical pulse in amplitude and timing to meet the input requirements of subsequent systems. High Power Microwave (HPM) sources require high voltage, high current pulse of short duration as its input for operation. This requirement of HPM sources is met through specialized configurations of PSN. It conditions/ shapes output of current source to a form suitable for driving high voltage pulse power loads. A typical configuration of PSN consists of Electrically Exploding Wire Opening Switch (EEW-OS)/ Fuse with inductor in series. A high current is passed through circuit. The fuse transforms from solid to vaporization phase by virtue of very high current flowing through it and its resistance increases sharply. This results in sharp fall in current leading to development of sharp rising high voltage pulse across inductor/fuse. The dynamic behavior of EEW-OS/ Fuse and its effect on modifying the input current is a complex relationship which governs the output characteristics of the circuit. This paper covers the implementation of dynamic behavior (dynamic resistivity/ resistance) of fuse along with complete circuit modelling and simulation involving current source, fuse and load, done using MATLAB/SIMULINK at Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory (TBRL). Benchmarking of the model has been done against the published results in literature and experimental results.

articleTitle: Optimal Non-convex Combined Heat and Power Economic Dispatch Using Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The economic scheduling of Combined Heat and Power (CHP) systems is a very hard and complex problem. With a rise in the number of operational units and related constraints, the conventional mathematical techniques cannot be used for optimization and optimal scheduling of the CHP units. This problem aims to simultaneously minimize the overall cost of operation of the electrical generator, CHP and heat generator units with the consideration of various operational constraints. This problem is very challenging and difficult to solve since the objective function is nonconvex and has nonlinear characteristics. A popular optimization technique, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is used in this paper to solve CHPED problem. The algorithm mimics the social behaviour and the food searching strategy of birds or fishes, which usually move in groups in search of food. To demonstrate the algorithm's superiority in handling different related constraints and the ability to produce better results, it is implemented on three different test systems. The results obtained by PSO on all the test systems are compared with the results obtained using some of the latest published techniques, which highlights the superiority of the PSO algorithm.

articleTitle: ICEFEET2020 Talks
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the tutorial presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Development of Linseed Oil Based Quartz Crystal Microbalance Sensor for Detection of Trimethylamine
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The present study aims to develop a linseed oil coated quartz crystal microbalance sensor to detect trimethylamine (TMA), an important freshness indicating agent of fish. The strong odor of TMA is often termed as “Fish odor”. It is likely to be generated when bacteria starts growing on dead fish. Therefore to detect TMA, a simple approach of vegetable oil film as a receptor element in the quartz crystal transduction platform has been elucidated herein. The developed sensor exhibits a significant sensitivity towards TMA with a sensitivity of 0.1841 kHz/ppm (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.92). Alongside, satisfactory repeatability, reproducibility, and selectivity of the prepared sensor have been studied successfully.

articleTitle: PID Control of a Fixed Displacement Electro-Hydrostatic Actuation System
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper presented the modeling and analysis of a Fixed Displacement Electro-Hydrostatic Actuation (FDEHA) system. The controlling of FDEHA systems is considered as viable alternatives to the conventional actuation control systems. Conventional actuators require a centralized hydraulic system, which constitutes a significant weight penalty and increased vulnerability. Fundamentally, an FDEHA system consists of the main actuator, manifold, variable speed motor, positive displacement pump, valves, and control electronics. For this study, a fixed displacement axial piston type bi-directional swash plate pump is used. This is since the suction and delivery manifolds switch their role with the reversal in direction of rotation. The motion of the asymmetric actuator is controlled by controlling the speed of the pump motor. An accumulator is used to ensure the cavitation free operation of the system.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting: A Hybrid Approach Using Data Mining Methods
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Load forecasting and analysis play a crucial role in electric power management and market planning of the grid system. In this paper, a hybrid approach using data mining methods is proposed for short term load forecasting. The approach uses the AFTER (Aggregated Forecast through Exponential Reweighting) algorithm to combine k-means clustering-Naive Bayes classification model and ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) model forecasts to form a hybrid model for load forecasting from the supply side. The error in the forecast from the hybrid model is also corrected and reduced using the neural network. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method a case study has been put through where load forecast is performed using actual load data from AEGCL (Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited), Assam. Load forecast is done for the first week of December 2012 and 2018 using training data set from January to November 2012 and 2018 respectively. The error of the forecast load is measured using MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error) to test the accuracy of the proposed method. The hybrid model forecast with the neural network error model extensively improves prediction accuracy of the load forecast from the supply side when compared to individual forecast models considered.

articleTitle: Study of Cognitive Fatigue using EEG Entropy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Cognitive fatigue may be induced by prolonged periods of continuous and repeated activity. The subsequent drop in alertness levels may be detected and analyzed by the use of physiological signals such as Electroencephalogram(EEG), ocular features, speech etc. The present paper employs entropy of EEG signals as a marker of cognitive fatigue and validates the results through performance of subjects in a set of standard neuropsychological tests. Correspondence observed in the trends may be considered indicative of gradual increase in fatigue levels with increase in cognitive loading.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption and Energy Saving Potential in Indian Textile Sector
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Energy is one of the major factors which are required for the development of any country. In our country India, the textile sector is one of the main consumer of energy among all industrial sectors. To conserve the energy in indian spinning textile industries; energy audit is performed which improve the energy efficiency with justified methodology and cost effective way. In this research study, the identified areas for energy conservation are- electricity bill analysis, power factor improvement, power quality analysis of supply mains, lighting system, ring frame three phase induction motors, compressed air system and rooftop solar PV system. A step-by-step procedure is also developed in this study for performing energy audit in an industry.

articleTitle: Secured Pulse Rate Monitoring System using IoT and Cloud
publicationTitle: 2020 International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: With a large fraction of deaths attributed to heart disorders, or specifically, cardiovascular diseases, there is an umpteen need to monitor the heart beat rate of individuals who are diagnosed as high risk individuals in a convenient fashion. Prior to a heart attack or anything detrimental to the condition of the human heart, the heart beat rate either shows a variation or an uphill or downhill gradient in its beat rate as found in medical studies. Thus we propose to keep a close watch for many such individuals altogether through a network of Internet of Things (IoT) and Cloud computing. The data of heart beat for an individual qualifies as private medical information for an individual and thus end to end encryption is facilitated through AES 128 scheme to ensure data privacy. To ensure a real-time monitoring, which would be both easily accessible and also secured, we designed android application based platform for communication of the health alerts and monitoring of the individual's condition in real time.
